## What you should be able to do tonight

- Say, for each of the deflated Sharpe, the probability of backtest overfitting and the reality check, what question it answers and what it needs as input.
- State which of the three you can compute honestly for your own research and which you cannot.

## Drill <span class='task-total'>interview thread</span>

Spaced repetition, not cramming. Every drill in the year is collected on the [drills page](../drills.qmd).

::: {.task-list .drill}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Arithmetic, timed, eighth sitting: ten two-digit multiplications, the sevenths, and 1/1.05 to four decimal places by long division in your head.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> The canonical urn-and-information problem: three cards, one red on both sides, one white on both sides, one red and white. You draw one at random and see red. Probability the other side is red? Say the wrong answer out loud first, then the right one, and name the mistake in the wrong one.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Expectation with a twist: you roll a fair die repeatedly and stop when you choose. Your payoff is the last roll. What is the optimal stopping rule and its expected value? Then do it for a payoff of the average of all rolls so far.
:::
:::
